_comment: ATMOSPHERE profiles (plan-region-atmosphere.md A1) — the AIR over an area, not the ground under it. Worn ONLY by zone.atmospheres; the ground is the sibling file, terrain-profiles.json. ⭐ The two tables are SEPARATE on purpose (PO 2026-09-15): they used to share one file and therefore one Tiled dropdown, so naming a ground profile on an atmosphere drew nothing and naming an atmosphere profile on a region painted grey mud — L15, and it cost a session. Now Tiled offers AuraAtmosphereProfile here and AuraProfile there, and neither mistake is a dropdown entry. ⚑ Same lookup engine, same D0 transparency rule, same D14 colour fallback as terrain — a profile is still just a named bag of presentation properties.
_comment_air: ⭐ THE AIR IS TWO THINGS, and which one you author decides how it behaves (PO 2026-09-14, replacing the single `gloom`). `darkness` is the ABSENCE OF LIGHT: a lantern removes it by definition, so it is drawn where the light holes erase it, and it is COLOUR ONLY — never textured, never drifting. `haze` is SUSPENDED MATTER (fog, smoke, dust): a lamp shows it to you rather than dispersing it, so it lives in its own layer that nothing erases, and it is the half that carries `texture`, `scale`, `blend` and `scroll`. ⛔ `haze` is NOT 'texture opacity' — it is the opacity of that whole LAYER, and it paints with or without a tile: author `haze` and no `texture` and the profile falls back to its `color` (D14) and paints a flat wash at that opacity. The key says WHICH LAYER your air lives in, never how strong a tile is. ⚑ Haze draws UNDER darkness, so fog is only visible where there is light to see it by — an unlit smoky cave reads black and its fog appears in the lantern pocket. ⭐ Authoring BOTH is the smoky cave and is supported; their opacities COMPOUND rather than max (0.8 darkness under 0.4 haze reads about 0.88 unlit). ⭐ `0` is NOT the same as omitting, and since A4 the difference is finally the intuitive one: `0` DECLARES that this air has none of that layer — it paints nothing and it stops the search, so a pure fog profile can say 'and it is not dark in here' — while omitting the key means no opinion and defers outward. ⛔ NEITHER erases. An ERASE is an AuraClearing, its own Tiled class with its own `zone.clearings` array and no profile at all; before A4 it was a profile authoring `darkness: 0`, one key doing two jobs (how much, and which operation), and the PO rejected that on sight. ⚑ Omitting still means the bank vanishes rather than going pale, which is the session that cost. ⚑ Every number here is [PLACEHOLDER] and is exactly what the look sitting is for.
_comment_sight: `sight` (plan-region-atmosphere.md A2) is how far the local player sees UNAIDED inside this air, in WORLD UNITS. Unlike the two dials above it resolves PER POINT at the player rather than per shape — §3.1 is why getting the two the wrong way round is the trap. ⭐ D7: it can only ever make a place KINDER, because the hole is max(wire light_radius, sight) and never a replacement, so an atmosphere cannot cancel a Lantern. For scale against a 20 x 12 unit screen: Lantern is r 4.0 (+0.5/level), Torch 2.5, a campfire 7.0 — so ~2 reads as 'grope forward' and much past ~8 stops being darkness at all. Nothing shipped authors it yet.
_comment_fog_tile: `fog-placeholder` is generated by tools/make-fog-tile.mjs (deterministic, re-runnable, seam proven rather than eyeballed), the same posture as the water tile. ⚑ It is the ONLY RGBA tile in the ground directory, on purpose: `haze` applies ONE opacity to a whole shape, so a fully opaque tile at haze 0.6 is a flat wash — the tile's own varying alpha is what gives thick banks and thin wisps inside a single authored polygon.
_comment_precipitation: ⭐ WEATHER IS `haze` — suspended matter you see BY light rather than the absence of it, so a lantern shows you the snow and never disperses it. That is why none of it needed a new key: precipitation is fog with discrete particles and a fast drift, and `texture` + `scroll` + `haze` already say exactly that. ⛔ NONE OF THESE AUTHOR `darkness`, and the omission is a decision rather than an oversight: a storm sky and a sandstorm are both legitimately dark, but `darkness` is the half a lantern ERASES, and rain inside a lit room should stay rain. Omitting means no opinion (D0), so weather over a dark cave mouth still reads dark, and a storm that wants a darkened sky COMPOSES — lay `Storm Sky` under the weather and both paint. See _comment_one_key_each for why that stack is the RIGHT way to say it and not a workaround. ⛔⛔ AND NONE AUTHOR `sight`, which is the trap worth writing down: `sight` is D7's `max(wire light_radius, sight)`, so it can only ever make a place KINDER. Authoring it on a blizzard or a sandstorm would make the player see FARTHER in it than in clear air — the exact opposite of the intent. No key shortens sight, and inventing one is a design ruling nobody has made. ⚑ `scroll` is the MOTION OF THE MEDIUM, not a breeze, and its magnitude is the whole difference between these: rain falls at 5.5 u/s, ash settles at 1.1, miasma creeps at 0.12, and fairy motes RISE (negative y). ⭐ For the two STREAK tiles (Rain, Sandstorm) it is also COUPLED TO THE TILE: make-precipitation-tiles.mjs reads each one's own `scroll` and leans its streaks along it, so re-tuning that drift means re-running the script or the rain slides sideways instead of falling. The dot tiles are round and do not care. ⛔ `Fairy Dust` is the one that does NOT fully work, and it is honest about it: motes should GLOW, but haze draws UNDER darkness, so in an unlit place they are invisible until something lights them — fine in an outdoor Magic Forest, wrong in a cave. And D9's one-vector-per-profile means the whole sheet drifts together, so it reads as a RISING DRIFT rather than independent fluttering. Two overlapping Fairy Dust-family banks drifting across each other is the authoring trick that buys back the shimmer. ⭐ `haze` READS AGAINST HOW FULL THE TILE IS, which is why `Fairy Dust` sits at 0.75 while `Sandstorm` sits at 0.5 and is the heavier air of the two. Haze multiplies the WHOLE tile, and empty pixels stay empty however high it goes — so on a SPARSE tile a high value buys bright, saturated marks on clear air, while on a full tile the same value is a wash over everything. Fairy dust covers under 10 % of its tile, so 0.75 makes the motes actually glow instead of blending halfway into the ground; the sandstorm covers 36 %, so 0.5 is already thick. ⛔ Reading `haze` as 'how strong is this weather' and sorting the numbers that way gets it backwards. ⚑ `blend` is 3 rather than the fog bank's 2 because a weather FRONT is a broader thing than a fog bank — [PLACEHOLDER], like every number here. ⚑ D14 still applies and is worth picturing: with the tile missing, a mostly-transparent precipitation tile falls back to a FLAT wash of its `color` at the full `haze` opacity, which is far heavier than the weather it stands in for. Every colour matches its tile's tint, so the hue does not jump when the texture lands.
_comment_one_key_each: ⭐ EVERY PROFILE BELOW DECLARES EXACTLY ONE of `darkness` and `haze`, and that is a rule rather than a coincidence — it is what makes stacking two banks safe. ⛔ THE DRAWING AND THE LOOKUP DISAGREE ABOUT OVERLAP, measured 2026-09-16, not assumed: `paintAtmospheres` walks EVERY shape and paints each into its own container, so two overlapping banks COMPOUND on screen — while `resolveIn` walks BACKWARD and returns the first shape that DECLARES the key, so the lookup picks exactly one and compounds nothing. Overlap two shapes that both declare `darkness` and the screen shows ~0.44 where the sim reads 0.3. ⚑ Today that is invisible, because the only consumer is `inDarkness()`, a `> 0` test that answers the same for every positive value — but a future consumer reading the MAGNITUDE would find the two sources disagreeing, so do not learn the wrong lesson from it being quiet. ⭐ One key each dodges it entirely: a darkness bank and a haze bank can overlap freely, because neither declares what the other does. That is why `Storm Sky` carries no haze and `Sandstorm` no darkness, however much a real sandstorm darkens the sky — THE STACK is how you say both (lay `Storm Sky` under `Sandstorm` and both paint), and it is strictly more expressive than one profile saying both, because the author picks the pairing per place.
_comment_darkness_family: The colour-only half — no tile, no drift, and a lantern erases all of it. ⚑ `color` is what the dark is MADE of, and it is worth authoring away from black: cave dark is black, but forest shade is green-black and a storm sky is blue-grey. A flat #000000 everywhere makes every dark place the same place. ⭐ `blend` IS READ HERE, since 2026-09-17 — it was haze's alone until then, so every dark bank drew with a hard polygon edge and there was no way to author it away. It is the ONE look key the two halves SHARE: `texture`, `scale` and `scroll` are still refused on this side by `paintAir`'s `flat` branch, because a profile authoring both keys would otherwise draw its tile twice and compound it against itself. ⚑ All four carry the same 2 on purpose — one [PLACEHOLDER] to judge before splitting them apart, and `Cave Air`'s wants judging beside the 2-unit `EDGE_FADE` rim on the `darkAreas` circles it will sit next to. ⛔ The band is SYMMETRIC about the authored polygon (D22, no inset), so a bank spills half a band past the shape drawn in Tiled — and `inDarkness()` still answers on the polygon itself, which puts the nameplate cut-off at the band's MIDPOINT rather than at its visible outer edge.
_comment_haze_family: The suspended-matter half — each carries its own tile, because D14 makes `color` a FALLBACK and NEVER a tint, so two profiles naming one tile are identical on screen and every distinct look costs a PNG. ⚑ The tiles come from two generators, split by what the air IS: `tools/make-fog-tile.mjs` builds DENSITY FIELDS (Fog, Miasma — a wave sum covering every pixel) and `tools/make-precipitation-tiles.mjs` builds PARTICLES (Rain, Snow, Ash Fall, Sandstorm, Fairy Dust — discrete marks on a mostly-empty tile). Each script carries one constant block per tile; a new one of either family is a block, not a script.
